subject: business-studies
title: Motivation Theories: Maslow and Herzberg
welcome_lead: From basic needs to two-factor theory - what really motivates people at work?
meta_desc: A-Level HR: Maslow's hierarchy and Herzberg's two-factor theory.
final_note: Pay alone removes dissatisfaction; growth and recognition produce real motivation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Maslow stacks needs in five levels: physiological, safety, social, esteem, and self-actualisation. People move up only when lower needs are reasonably met.
Herzberg argued hygiene factors stop dissatisfaction but do not motivate; motivators like recognition and growth actively drive performance. Doubling pay rarely lifts motivation for long.
Job enrichment adds Herzberg motivators by widening responsibility. Enlargement just adds tasks at the same level and fails to motivate by itself.

Hygiene factors (pay, conditions, policies) prevent dissatisfaction when present but don't motivate; motivators (recognition, achievement, responsibility) create positive satisfaction.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
